history.summary: Old Shiva temple in the Mahadeva locality of Siwan town housing a rare panchmukhi (five-faced) Shivalinga. Local tradition holds that the lingam emerged from the earth (swayambhu), and devotees also discern the faces of Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh on it. The temple draws hundreds of devotees daily and hosts a fair on Mahashivratri. UNVERIFIED: no reliable source documents the temple's founding date or dynasty. Coordinates are approximate (Siwan town centre; the temple itself is not individually geocoded). No verified photograph of this temple was found after three image searches.

town_description: Siwan is the district headquarters of Siwan district in northwestern Bihar, set on the banks of the Daha river. It is a regional commercial and administrative hub, and the gateway to nearby Ziradei, the birthplace of India's first president Dr. Rajendra Prasad, and to Ashiana, the preserved home of freedom fighter Maulana Mazharul Haq. The town has a subtropical climate with hot summers and mild winters.
